chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him):
Regarding a man who is asked, 'Have you divorced your wife?' and he says, 'Yes,' he said, 'He has divorced her at that time.'
ai.seo_question: When does a divorce take effect if a man is asked and simply says 'Yes'?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarifies the legal mechanism of 'declaration by affirmation' (al-taqrir), establishing that a man's simple 'Yes' to the question 'Did you divorce your wife?' constitutes an immediate, binding divorce. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the efficacy of the husband's intent conveyed through concise speech, distinguishing it from conditional or delayed divorces. It serves as a foundational precedent for understanding how verbal confirmation alone can trigger the legal status of talaq without requiring explicit phrasing of the divorce formula.
